tools.name: wait
tools.description:
Waits on a yielded `exec` cell and returns new output or completion.
- Use `wait` only after `exec` returns `Script running with cell ID ...`.
- `cell_id` identifies the running `exec` cell to resume.
- `yield_time_ms` controls how long to wait for more output before yielding again. Defaults to 10000 ms.
- `max_tokens` limits how much new output this wait call returns. Defaults to 10000 tokens.
- `terminate: true` stops the running cell; false or omitted waits for output.
- `wait` returns only the new output since the last yield, or the final completion or termination result for that cell.
- If the cell is still running, `wait` may yield again with the same `cell_id`.
- If the cell has already finished, `wait` returns the completed result and closes the cell.

cell_id.description: Identifier of the running exec cell.

max_tokens.description: Output token budget for this wait call. Defaults to 10000 tokens.

terminate.description: True stops the running exec cell; false or omitted waits for output.

yield_time_ms.description: Wait before yielding more output. Defaults to 10000 ms.

        Spawns an agent to work on the specified task. If your current task is `/root/task1` and you spawn_agent with task_name "task_3" the agent will have canonical task name `/root/task1/task_3`.

tools.name: js
tools.description:
Control native apps or browsers on the user’s computer by reading or operating UI. Prefer purpose-built skills, connectors, APIs, or CLIs when available.

On the first invocation of `cua_repl`, or after resetting it, execute exactly one of the API calls shown below, optionally assigning its result to a variable. Do not add other API calls, waits, or snapshots to that invocation.
The tool result will include documentation and, when creating or selecting a tab or selecting an app, its initial UI state. Selecting a browser does not open a tab. Read that result before continuing.
Use only APIs described in the tool instructions or returned documentation.

When you need an inventory of available apps, browsers, and tabs, get a snapshot of all enabled surfaces. Otherwise, use the relevant entry point below:

```javascript
await cua.getState();
```

Use the first matching browser control option from the user's request:

For a tab @-mention (`mention=tab-v1`):
Pass the complete `plugin://...` URL to get the referenced tab.

```javascript
let tab = await cua.getTab({ mention: tabMentionUrl });
```

For an existing tab identified by URL in browser context (including the current IAB tab):

```javascript
let tab = await cua.getTab({ url }, { browser: browserId });
```

Known tab ID (`tabId` or `providerTabId`) and browser (name or browser @-mention):

```javascript
let tab = await cua.getTab(tabId, { browser: browserId });
```

To open a URL in the in-app browser (`@Browser`):

```javascript
let tab = await cua.createBrowserTab("iab", url, { visible: boolean });
```

To open a URL in another named browser: pass its name directly; do not call `getBrowser` first.

```javascript
let tab = await cua.createBrowserTab(browserName, url, browserOptions);
```

Known URL, only when the user has not specified a browser by name or @-mention:

```javascript
let browser = await cua.getBrowser({ url });
```

Browser IDs and options:

- `"mcpapps"`: use `cua.getBrowser({ id: "mcpapps" })` for existing full-screen MCP Apps in the task’s side panel.
- `"iab"` (in-app browser): in `createBrowserTab`, use `visible: true` to show the browser; `false` to keep it hidden.
- `"dot"` (Dot): use only when present in browser inventory. It accesses tabs on Dot's active main thread. `cua.getTab(tabId, { browser: "dot" })` selects an existing tab. `cua.createBrowserTab("dot", url, { visible: boolean })` creates one with the same visibility options as `"iab"`.
- `"chrome"` (@Chrome), `"edge"` (@Edge): pass a short, emoji-prefixed `sessionName` (e.g. `"🔎 Task"`) to `createBrowserTab` when starting a task.

If the user specifies an app to use, get the app by name, bundle ID, or path:

```javascript
let app = await cua.getApp("Example App");
```

To add other content to the tool result, use `nodeRepl.write(value)` for text or other values and `await nodeRepl.emitImage(image)` for images. The APIs listed above already display their documentation or UI state; do not wrap their results in `write` or `emitImage`.

If your context begins with a summary of an existing computer use task, call `await cua.rewriteDocumentation()` before continuing the computer use task to ensure you have a complete view of the necessary documentation.

Each `cua_repl.js` call opens or continues a browser activity. Keep consecutive calls together. The activity stays open across messages until you emit completion commentary.

**Manual takeover takes priority over the table below.** For a required manual browser step, call the documented takeover API before asking the user to act, unless takeover is already pending. Explain the required step in your final reply. Tab marking alone does not transfer control. While waiting for the user to finish and return control, emit no completion and make no CUA calls, even when answering side questions. The takeover API returning does not end this wait. When the user returns or unblocks you, resume browser work and apply the table. If they cancel, replace, or no longer need the browser work, close the activity before answering, even without another CUA call.

Completion is a standalone assistant commentary message containing only `::browser-complete{title="<headline>"}`. Never put it in a tool call or final reply. Use 3–6 words starting with a past-tense verb to describe the observed outcome. Omit identifiers.

After a user cancels pending browser work: commentary `::browser-complete{title="Stopped browser work"}`, then the final acknowledgement. No browser call is needed.

For an open browser activity:

| Next action                                   | Required output order                                                                     |
| --------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Another CUA call                              | Continue without completion.                                                              |
| A non-CUA tool, final reply, or chat question | Finish required tab marking, emit completion, then take that action in the same response. |

With no open activity, emit no completion. Later CUA use requires a fresh completion at the next table boundary.

If you need a one-time sign-in code, information, or confirmation from the user, follow the table and ask in chat. One-time code entry alone does not require takeover. This tool is part of plugin `unified-computer-use`.

code.description: JavaScript to execute using the initialized cua_repl runtime.

timeout_ms.description: Optional execution timeout in milliseconds. Defaults to 30000 (30 seconds) when omitted.

title.description: Short user-facing description of what this code block is doing. Prefer a few words in present-progressive form, such as 'Checking the mobile layout' or 'Comparing prices', over imperative or past-tense titles.

tools.name: js_reset
tools.description: Reset the persistent cua_repl JavaScript session. All JavaScript bindings are discarded. The next cua_repl.js call initializes a fresh runtime for the enabled surfaces. This does not close browser tabs or native apps, or erase their state. This tool is part of plugin `unified-computer-use`.

     1	# Bulk CSV inventory import
     2	
     3	- **Author** — Alex Callow
     4	- **Status** — Proposed
     5	- **Date** — 2026-11-26
     6	
     7	## Overview
     8	
     9	Inventory operators can upload `inventory_frame.csv` from the running application and see the result as the job progresses. A routine update changes only the frames named in the file. An authoritative snapshot can also retire missing frames within a declared area of the inventory. Every accepted change is visible in frame history.
    10	
    11	## The Problem
    12	
    13	The application supports individual frame edits, but operators receive inventory updates as CSV files. Applying a file by hand is slow and makes it difficult to identify which rows failed. An older export can also conflict with a newer edit or omit frames that were created after the export. Operators need to apply the file, see what was accepted or skipped, and understand why a frame changed.
    14	
    15	## Goals
    16	
    17	- Let an authorized operator upload the supplied 45-field CSV from the application and see job progress, final counts, and actionable row errors.
    18	- Apply `DELTA` by default. Leave absent frames alone, preserve newer edits unless the operator explicitly forces a conflicting change, and avoid duplicate frame versions and events on retry or re-upload of unchanged rows.
    19	- Support `FULL_SNAPSHOT` for a single declared scope. Require country and region for environment-level scopes. Protect frames present in malformed rows, frames changed after the export watermark, and partitions with newer snapshots. Prevent retirement when the malformed-row rate exceeds 5% and abort before inventory writes if more than 10% of scoped active frames would retire.
    20	- Preserve accepted versions, source timestamps, and import lineage so operators can trace updates, forced corrections, and retirements.
    21	
    22	## Non-Goals
    23	
    24	- Hard deletion of inventory during import.
    25	- Arbitrary CSV schemas, field mapping, or automatic repair of malformed values.
    26	- A single snapshot covering several separately named scopes in the first release. Operators can submit separate regional snapshots or use `DELTA` for a cross-region update.
    27	
    28	## Technical Plan (Architecture)
    29	
    30	### Upload and dispatch
    31	
    32	```text
    33	Operator → web app → BFF → Spring Boot → import_jobs
    34	Operator → presigned PUT → S3 → SQS standard queue → Spring Boot → Temporal
    35	                                   SQS retries → DLQ → dispatch reconciler
    36	Temporal worker → pinned S3 object → PostgreSQL staging → inventory apply
    37	Inventory apply → frame versions + job outcome
    38	Operator ← web app ← BFF ← Spring Boot job status and row errors
    39	```
    40	
    41	The job creation API takes the import mode, optional snapshot scope and export watermark, and explicit force flag. Spring Boot validates the requested scope and permissions, creates an AWAITING_UPLOAD job, and returns its ID and the presigned PUT details through the BFF. The upload key is uploads/{jobId}/inventory_frame.csv. Use a create-only PUT and persist the accepted S3 object version so all retries read the same bytes. Expose job status, counts, fatal errors, and paginated row errors through the BFF.
    42	
    43	Configure S3 to send object-created notifications for the uploads/ prefix directly to a standard SQS queue in the same AWS Region. Grant the bucket permission to publish through a queue policy scoped to the bucket ARN and owner account. The Spring Boot consumer handles the native S3 notification envelope, recognizes the S3 test event, and processes each object record. It decodes the key and verifies the bucket, key, object version, and size, then conditionally records PENDING and starts Temporal workflow csv-import-{jobId}. Duplicate or out-of-order records must preserve the existing object binding and job state. Acknowledge the message after each applicable record has been handled, including confirming successful or already-completed workflow dispatch. If processing a later record fails, replay of earlier records uses the same job and workflow identities. Retry with backoff. Before a DLQ event can fail a job, reconcile ambiguous workflow starts and check that the job is still dispatchable. Reconcile old AWAITING_UPLOAD and PENDING jobs against S3 and Temporal.
    44	
    45	### Staging and validation
    46	
    47	Accept files up to 10 MiB and 10,000 data rows, whichever limit is reached first. Verify object size before dispatch and enforce both limits while streaming. The header does not count. Exceeding either limit fails the job before inventory writes. Keep uploaded object versions and row diagnostics for 7 days. Keep the minimal durable job outcome and import lineage available to history after diagnostics expire. Bound retries and reconciliation within the object retention period.
    48	
    49	Interpret the CSV created_date and modified_date fields as UTC at their supplied precision. Use UTC for source_modified_at storage and explicitly interpret the existing offset-free PostgreSQL column as UTC regardless of the database session timezone. Convert source timestamps to instants for watermark and manual-edit comparisons.
    50	
    51	The Temporal worker reads the pinned object and streams logical CSV records into job- and attempt-scoped UNLOGGED staging. Heartbeats report progress and let the worker detect cancellation. Keep the EOF completion marker in the same unlogged storage as the data. Before apply, check the marker and staged counts. If a crash leaves staging incomplete or empty, reload from S3. Store row errors with stable job, row, and error keys for retries. Track identifiable frame IDs independently of row validity. Hash canonical typed frame values with SHA-256 over a versioned, ordered encoding. Preserve meaningful text, normalize typed numeric values by value, encode null distinctly, order external references by type, and preserve the position of links. Exclude job metadata, version validity, and source timestamps from the payload hash. Compare hashes using the same encoding version. After staging, reject every row for a frame ID that appears more than once, report DUPLICATE_FRAME_ID for each duplicate row, and keep the ID in the snapshot presence set. Count each rejected logical record once toward the malformed-row threshold, even if it has several validation errors.
    52	
    53	### Inventory and history
    54	
    55	Use the existing frame table for stable identity and frame_version for current and historical values. Resolve region, town, postcode, and format through existing lookup tables. Attach external references and ordered links to the resulting frame version. Add job, row error, scope watermark, and import lineage storage through Flyway. Map the complete CSV to the existing model, including site and spec fields on frame_version. The BFF, protobuf service definitions, Spring service, and worker need changes for job creation, progress, and application.
    56	
    57	Re-read the current version under the existing stable-frame lock. A newer source timestamp creates a version. Equal timestamp and hash is a no-op. Skip and report stale rows and same-timestamp collisions unless forceOverwrite is authorized and set, and record both hashes for collisions. Manual writes set source_modified_at from database statement time after locking, and CSV writes preserve the input timestamp. For existing manual versions that inherited their source timestamp, use the version’s valid_from as the effective conflict baseline. Identify those versions at migration time and preserve the original source_modified_at for history. Forced corrections record FORCED_OVERWRITE and import_job_id. Subsequent imports compare against the current version’s source timestamp, including when a forced overwrite moves that timestamp backward. For example, an 11:00 row is newer after a forced overwrite replaces a 12:00 version with a 10:00 version. Use the same database-generated boundary for closing and opening a version, strictly later than the previous valid_from.
    58	
    59	When a frame has no current version and its latest version was closed by MANUAL_DELETE, require an authorized forceOverwrite to restore it in either import mode. Without that flag, skip the row and record MANUALLY_DELETED in the job’s row errors. With it, append a new current version, preserve the CSV source timestamp, and record FORCED_OVERWRITE and import_job_id in the apply transaction. Compare and restore under the stable-frame lock.
    60	
    61	Promote a complete staging attempt in one transaction. Acquire the job lock and verify eligibility before writing. Use one source candidate per target key and MERGE RETURNING where it fits. Close current versions and append replacements in separate set-based statements. Commit inventory, versioned references and links, the applicable scope watermark, and job result together. If the worker loses the commit response, return the stored result when it retries.
    62	
    63	### Snapshot apply
    64	
    65	Keep staging outside the inventory lock. During promotion, take a shared transaction-scoped inventory lock for manual writes and DELTA and an exclusive lock for FULL_SNAPSHOT. Obtain frame locks in stable ID order. Evaluate scope membership, watermark checks, and retirement against the protected pre-apply view.
    66	
    67	Require scope to be GLOBAL or a canonical country, country/region, or country/region/environment path. Use the explicit snapshot_as_of where available, otherwise derive it from MAX(modified_date) on the complete file. Check freshness and reject watermarks below the greatest committed value for the scope or its ancestors. A broader snapshot can still apply its present rows under the ordinary conflict rules when a descendant has a newer watermark. Protect that entire descendant subtree from retirement.
    68	
    69	Before writing inventory, fail the entire snapshot for a header-only file, an incomplete export, or an unrecoverable CSV parse error. Also fail the snapshot if any row has no recoverable frame ID or any record is outside the declared scope. Keep job diagnostics and leave inventory and the scope watermark unchanged. Count any identifiable frame ID in the CSV as present, including when other fields are malformed. Among absent active frames, exclude protected child scopes and current versions whose valid_from or source_modified_at exceeds the export watermark. Record SKIPPED_RETIREMENT_NEWER_THAN_SNAPSHOT for the latter. If eligible retirements exceed 10% of all active frames in the declared scope, fail before inventory writes. If more than 5% of CSV rows are malformed, fail the entire snapshot before writing inventory. Keep the job diagnostics and leave the scope watermark unadvanced. Represent each accepted retirement with a new RETIRED version and MISSING_FROM_FULL_SNAPSHOT. Advance only the incoming scope watermark on a successful commit.
    70	
    71	Exclude snapshot-retired frames from the default inventory list. Expose them through an explicit retired filter, direct lookup, and frame history.
    72	
    73	A FULL_SNAPSHOT can reactivate an unchanged row when the current version was retired with MISSING_FROM_FULL_SNAPSHOT, the incoming export watermark is strictly later than that retirement version’s valid_from, and the row’s source timestamp and canonical payload hash match the last live version. Append a new live version in the apply transaction. Apply normal conflict rules to other rows and to DELTA imports.
    74	
    75	## Alternatives Considered
    76	
    77	### Forward S3 notifications through Lambda
    78	
    79	A Lambda bridge can normalize events or route them to several destinations. The import has a single queue, and Spring Boot can consume the native event. The bridge adds a deployment and another delivery failure path.
    80	
    81	**Rejected by author** — Send S3 notifications directly to the standard SQS queue to remove the forwarding hop.
    82	
    83	### Use logged staging
    84	
    85	Logged staging can survive a PostgreSQL restart or failover and avoids downloading and parsing the same object again after staging is lost. It adds write-ahead logging and storage work for intermediate rows. The initial design uses UNLOGGED staging with replay from the pinned S3 object. Measure the cost of both approaches at the maximum supported upload size before committing to larger files.
    86	
    87	### Migrate to the six-table inventory model and separate frame history
    88	
    89	Separate site and spec entities would give those concepts independent identities and lifecycles. A migration would also change existing inventory reads and writes and would need to preserve historical values when site or spec records change.
    90	
    91	**Rejected by author** — Extend the existing versioned schema for this release. It already gives current and historical frames one authoritative store and preserves links and external references per version. A separate history store would add a second representation of those changes.

# Bulk CSV inventory import

Author: Alex Callow
Date: 2026-11-26

## Overview

An inventory operator uploads inventory_frame.csv directly to S3 using a presigned URL. The BFF delegates job creation to Spring Boot, which records AWAITING_UPLOAD and assigns uploads/{jobId}/inventory_frame.csv. An S3-triggered Lambda sends the upload event to SQS. Spring Boot moves the job to PENDING and starts Temporal workflow csv-import-{jobId}. SQS retries failed delivery and a DLQ listener records dispatch failures.

The worker streams the CSV into job-scoped UNLOGGED PostgreSQL staging in batches and heartbeats during loading. It records invalid rows in import_row_errors and applies set-based writes with MERGE RETURNING where appropriate. The proposed six-table target and frame history must be reconciled with the repository's existing versioned schema. Inventory changes and outbox records must commit together.

## Agreed import behavior

- A newer source timestamp creates a version. An equal timestamp and matching content hash is a no-op. An older timestamp produces STALE_RECORD. An equal timestamp with different content produces TIMESTAMP_COLLISION_CONFLICT and records both hashes. Skipped conflicts result in COMPLETED_WITH_ERRORS.
- The explicit forceOverwrite flag accepts stale and same-timestamp conflicts. The new version preserves source_modified_date and records FORCED_OVERWRITE and import_job_id. Close and open at one database-generated boundary strictly later than the locked current valid_from.
- DELTA is the default and leaves absent frames alone. FULL_SNAPSHOT requires an explicit GLOBAL scope or validated partition scope using country, region or environment. Every identifiable frame ID in the file counts as present, including rows with invalid payloads.
- FULL_SNAPSHOT soft-retires absent active frames in scope with MISSING_FROM_FULL_SNAPSHOT. Abort if more than 10% of scoped active frames would retire. A malformed-row rate above 5% must prevent retirement. Whether to fail the whole snapshot is open.

## Analysis

All seven Goldfish lenses completed review. The recommendations below are proposed decisions for RFC alignment.

### Delivery and recovery

- Bind each job to one immutable object. Sign the exact key and the create-only PUT condition (If-None-Match: *), enable S3 versioning, and persist the accepted version ID so every retry reads the same bytes. Keep the object through the retry and reconciliation window. Validate the bucket, decoded key, object version, and size before dispatch. [S3 conditional writes](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/conditional-writes.html) [S3 event delivery](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/notification-how-to-event-types-and-destinations.html)
- Record PENDING conditionally, invoke Temporal with the job-derived workflow ID, and acknowledge SQS only after start or after confirming the same job's workflow already exists. Configure both running-ID conflict and closed-ID reuse policies. A crash between the DB write and Temporal start leaves a retryable PENDING job. A lost start response must be reconciled before any DLQ transition to FAILED. Guard terminal states and fence a late starter with conditional job transitions before it can apply inventory. Reconcile old AWAITING_UPLOAD and PENDING jobs against S3 and Temporal, and cover Lambda delivery failures separately from consumer DLQ failures. [Temporal workflow ID policies](https://docs.temporal.io/develop/java/nexus/development-walkthrough/send-messages)
- Stage by job ID, attempt generation, and logical CSV row number. Record observed frame IDs independently of row validity. Mark a generation complete only after EOF and verify that its completion marker and counts still match before applying. Keep the marker in unlogged storage with the staged rows so recovery clears both, and reload from the bound S3 version when the marker is missing. Use heartbeats for liveness and cancellation. Restart the stream for an incomplete generation in the first release. Record row errors durably with stable keys so retries do not duplicate errors. [PostgreSQL unlogged tables](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/sql-createtable.html)

### Inventory apply

- Reuse the existing stable-frame lock, current-version uniqueness constraint, and close-and-append history. The repository already computes a boundary as the greater of database wall-clock time and the current valid_from plus one microsecond, then uses that boundary for the next version. Reuse this rule for all imported changes, including retirements. Preserve source_modified_at separately. The existing schema already stores versioned external references and links. Map each of the 45 CSV fields before adding new tables or moving attributes. Keep immutable history when normalizing shared site or spec data. [Schema](../frame-inventory-schema/frame-inventory-schema.md) [Repository](../../src/backend/src/main/java/com/global/ct/frameinventory/frame/FrameRepository.java)
- Define the content hash over canonical typed values, including versioned links and external references. Specify normalization, timezone and precision, null behavior, and duplicate-ID handling. - Persist snapshot_as_of on the job. Accept a producer-supplied export watermark at job creation. When omitted, derive it from MAX(modified_date) after scanning the complete file. Use one documented source timezone and precision for comparisons. Require the exporter to supply an explicit watermark when the file cannot establish one. MAX(modified_date) measures the newest row change and can lag the time a complete export was generated. It also cannot prove completeness, so prefer the explicit export watermark for feeds where these times differ.
- Use canonical scope keys in a containment hierarchy: GLOBAL, country, country/region, and country/region/environment. A failed job leaves all watermarks as they were.

This protects newer current versions, including edits within the same scope. Count only eligible retirements in the 10% numerator and keep the denominator as all pre-apply active frames in the declared scope. Capture the watermark checks, both exclusion counts, the breaker calculation, and the scope watermark update in the same protected apply transaction.

The agreed representation is a new current version with status RETIRED and reason MISSING_FROM_FULL_SNAPSHOT. Define how current inventory queries treat that version and how a later import reactivates it. Existing manual deletion closes the last current version without opening a replacement. ## Goals and non-goals

- Deliver authenticated upload, visible job progress and row errors, retry-safe imports, audited versions, scoped retirement, and transactional outbox records.
- Leave mass deletion, generalized CSV mapping, automatic repair of malformed source values, and multi-scope FULL_SNAPSHOT uploads outside the first release. If authoritative cross-region exports become a regular need, consider one atomic job over explicitly named scopes, each with its own watermark and retirement check.

## Alternatives weighed

- Keep the S3-to-Lambda bridge as requested. Direct S3-to-SQS delivery could remove an operational failure path if the bridge only forwards events. Verify what routing or event normalization the Lambda needs to own.
- Keep UNLOGGED staging with full source replay for initial implementation. Durable staging could reduce replay cost and operational complexity after failover, at the cost of logging intermediate data. Benchmark with the expected maximum file.
- Reuse versioned history as the initial design direction. Add a separate frame_history table only if it serves a distinct audited need. Otherwise two history stores would require agreement on which is authoritative.

## Key decisions and implementation sequence

1. Map the CSV to the current schema and the proposed six entities. Resolve source timestamp parsing, manual-edit ordering, force authorization, link semantics, duplicate IDs, and schema ownership before migrations.
2. Add durable job, row error, lineage, and outbox storage through additive Flyway migrations. Expose BFF job creation and status, including counts, fatal errors, and paginated row errors. Set upload-size, row-count, timeout, and retention limits from the agreed operating envelope.
3. Implement the S3 event bridge, SQS dispatch and DLQ, and Temporal start. Exercise duplicate notifications, late events, ambiguous starts, and reconciliation before applying inventory.
4. Implement staging and atomic DELTA apply. Run the supplied CSV against PostgreSQL 18 and check replay, timestamp collisions, manual edits, forced overwrite, malformed quoting, duplicate IDs, lost staging, and worker failure immediately after commit.
5. Add scoped FULL_SNAPSHOT with a protected retirement calculation. Verify that malformed rows with IDs stay present, out-of-scope frames stay untouched, and the exact 5% and 10% boundaries behave as agreed. Exercise rejection of environment scopes without a region, expired and out-of-order watermarks, watermark equality, derived watermarks, newer ancestors rejecting narrower snapshots, newer descendants protecting entire subtrees while present rows still upsert, frames created or moved into scope after export, and concurrent manual writes. Roll out DELTA first, then enable snapshot after observing apply times and reviewing operator safeguards.
6. Track queue age and DLQ depth, time in each job state, staging retries, apply transaction duration, row error codes, retirement guard trips, and outbox lag. Correlate logs by job ID and keep presigned URLs and raw row content out of logs.

## Overview

The backend is a Java 21 Spring Boot application. Spring gRPC serves frame management on port 9090. Spring MVC and Actuator serve health endpoints on port 8080. Spring Boot applies Flyway migrations against PostgreSQL at startup. The Docker image builds a Spring Boot JAR and runs it on Java 21. ## Subdirectories & Boundaries

- [Source tree](./src/README.md) contains the application and its runtime configuration.
- [Inventory migration](./src/main/resources/db/migration/V1__create_frame_inventory.sql) creates the frame, version history, and related tables.
- [Frame inventory schema](../../docs/frame-inventory-schema/frame-inventory-schema.md) maps the CSV fields and describes the shared Spring write transaction.

## Local development

Start the Compose PostgreSQL service from the repository root with
`docker compose up -d --wait postgres`. From `src/backend`, run
`./gradlew bootRun` with Java 21. The local JDBC defaults connect to the
Compose database. Set `SPRING_DATASOURCE_URL`, `SPRING_DATASOURCE_USERNAME`,
and `SPRING_DATASOURCE_PASSWORD` when connecting to a different database.

## Verification

From `src/backend`, run `./gradlew test` with Java 21 and Docker available. The
suite covers unit tests and calls the gRPC service through a generated client
against PostgreSQL 18.6 using Testcontainers. Flyway applies both schema
migrations during the integration tests.

## Frame management API

The [Protobuf definition](src/main/proto/frameinventory/v1/frames.proto) declares
the six RPCs. Run `./gradlew generateProto` to generate the Java messages and
stubs. The [API contract](../../docs/frame-management-grpc-api.md#grpc-contract) describes
pagination, request fields, errors, and version checks.

With the backend running, call the service from `src/backend` using `grpcurl`.

```sh
grpcurl -plaintext -import-path src/main/proto -proto frameinventory/v1/frames.proto \
  -d '{"page":0,"size":25}' localhost:9090 frameinventory.v1.FrameManagement/ListFrames
```

The backend writes structured JSON logs to the console. Set
`LOGGING_LEVEL_COM_GLOBAL_CT_FRAMEINVENTORY_FRAME=DEBUG` to include frame RPC
parameters, version checks, lookup results, and handled client errors.

## Sentry error reporting

Set `SENTRY_DSN` to the DSN of the backend's Sentry project and set
`SENTRY_ENVIRONMENT` to the environment name, such as `staging`. The environment
defaults to `local`. An empty or unset DSN disables error reporting.

Export the variables before running `./gradlew bootRun` from `src/backend`.
For Docker Compose, export the same variables or set them in an untracked
`.env` file at the repository root, then run `docker compose up --build -d backend`
to rebuild and apply the settings.

To verify reporting, use a non-production Sentry project or environment. In a
local checkout, temporarily make a controller handler throw an
`IllegalStateException` with a unique test message and call that route. Confirm
the event appears in Sentry with the expected stack trace and environment tag,
then link the event on the issue. Remove the temporary exception and confirm
`curl --fail http://localhost:8080/api/health` succeeds with the DSN configured
and again after restarting the backend with the DSN unset.

When you’re developing cloud and serverless applications, you need to grant access to various AWS resources like S3 buckets and RDS databases.

Conclusion
Section titled “Conclusion”
IAM Policy Stream streamlines your development process by minimizing the manual creation of policies and confirming the necessity of granted permissions.
However, it is advisable to manually confirm that your policy aligns with your intended actions.
Your code may unintentionally make requests, and LocalStack considers all requests made during policy generation as valid.
A practical scenario is automating tests, such as integration or end-to-end testing, against your application using LocalStack.
This setup allows LocalStack to automatically generate policies with the required permissions.
However, it’s important to note that these generated policies may not cover all possible requests, as only the requests made during testing are included.
You can then review and customize the policies to meet your needs, ensuring that overly permissive policies don’t find their way into production environments.

Section titled “Why use IAM Policy Stream?” LocalStack enables you to create and enforce local IAM roles and policies using the ENFORCE_IAM feature . It’s important to find a balance, avoiding giving too many permissions while making sure the right ones are granted. This challenge becomes more complex when dealing with AWS services that make requests not directly visible to users. For instance, if an SNS topic sends a message to an SQS queue and the underlying call fails, there might be no clear error message, causing confusion, especially for those less familiar with the services. IAM Policy Stream simplifies this by automatically generating the needed policies and showing them to users. # Frame Inventory

Monorepo scaffold for the frame-inventory take-home exercise.

## System Overview

The Next.js page calls the Spring Boot health endpoint through a same-origin rewrite. Docker Compose runs both modules alongside PostgreSQL, OpenSearch, OpenSearch Dashboards, Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, Alloy, and the OpenTelemetry Collector. The exercise provides a legacy export in `data/inventory_frame.csv` and describes the inventory features in `INSTRUCTIONS.md`.

Bring the whole stack up with one command.

```bash
docker compose up --build
```

Once PostgreSQL is healthy, the backend applies pending Flyway migrations during startup.

If you have `just` installed, run `just` to list the available recipes.

| Command | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| `just up` | Build and start the whole stack in the foreground. |
| `just down` | Stop the stack and retain its named data volumes. |
| `just compose logs -f backend` | Pass arguments through to Docker Compose. |
| `just migrate` | Run Flyway on its own in a one-off backend container. |

## Subdirectories & System Boundaries

- [Application source](./src/README.md) contains the Spring Boot backend, Apollo Server BFF, and Next.js frontend.
- [Design system](./design-system/README.md) contains the prototype, sample frame data, and visual conventions for the exercise.

## Services

`docker compose up` starts the following services.

| Service               | Host port | Container port | Notes                                                  |
|-----------------------|-----------|----------------|--------------------------------------------------------|
| frontend              | 3000      | 3000           | Next.js dev server, proxies `/api` to the backend     |
| bff                   | 4000      | 4000           | Apollo Sandbox and the frame inventory GraphQL API     |
| backend               | 8080      | 8080           | Spring Boot, exposes `GET /api/health`                 |
| postgres              | 5432      | 5432           | Spring Boot applies the inventory schema via Flyway    |
| opensearch            | 9200, 9600 | 9200, 9600    | Single-node, security plugin disabled for local use    |
| opensearch-dashboards | 5601      | 5601           | UI for the OpenSearch cluster above                    |
| prometheus            | 9091      | 9090           | Scrapes Spring Boot and Apollo metrics every 15 seconds |
| otel-collector        | 9464      | 9464           | Scrapes Spring Boot metrics for local inspection       |
| grafana               | 3001      | 3000           | Queries provisioned Prometheus and Loki data            |

### Credentials

| Service               | User       | Password       | Database         |
|-----------------------|------------|----------------|------------------|
| postgres              | `app`      | `app`          | `frames`         |
| opensearch            | n/a        | n/a            | n/a              |
| grafana               | `admin`    | `admin`         | n/a              |

## Global Invariants

- The Next.js rewrite preserves the `/api/` path and uses `BACKEND_URL` as its destination origin. Compose sets it to `http://backend:8080`. `[src/frontend/next.config.ts:rewrites]` `[docker-compose.yml:services.frontend.environment.BACKEND_URL]`
- The health page expects `status`, `service`, and `timestamp` from `GET /api/health`. The backend supplies those fields directly. `[src/frontend/src/app/page.tsx:HealthResponse]` `[src/backend/src/main/java/com/global/ct/frameinventory/HealthController.java:health]`

## Global Side Effects

- Opening the frontend requests `/api/health`, which the Next.js server forwards to the backend. The response reports the current time from the backend clock. `[src/frontend/src/app/page.tsx:Home]` `[src/frontend/next.config.ts:rewrites]` `[src/backend/src/main/java/com/global/ct/frameinventory/HealthController.java:health]`
- Docker Compose publishes service ports and creates named volumes for PostgreSQL and OpenSearch. OpenSearch Dashboards connects to OpenSearch on the Compose network. `[docker-compose.yml:services]` `[docker-compose.yml:volumes]` `[docker-compose.yml:services.opensearch-dashboards.environment.OPENSEARCH_HOSTS]`

## System Verification

- From `src/backend`, run `./gradlew test`.
- From `src/frontend`, run `npm run lint` after installing dependencies.

### Git hooks

Install [pre-commit](https://pre-commit.com/#installation), then run `pre-commit install`
from the repository root to install both Git hooks. The `pre-commit` hook checks
YAML, JSON, and merge conflict markers, and runs ESLint when staged changes touch
`src/frontend/`. Install the frontend dependencies with `npm ci --prefix src/frontend`
before committing frontend changes.

The `commit-msg` hook uses Commitlint to enforce the Conventional Commits format
documented in [AGENTS.md](./AGENTS.md). Commitlint requires Node.js 22.12 or newer.

Run `pre-commit run --all-files` to check the whole repository.

### Smoke test

Once the stack is up, check the service entry points.

- Open <http://localhost:3000> — the page calls `/api/health` and prints the JSON response.
- Hit the backend directly: <http://localhost:8080/api/health>.
- Open [Apollo Sandbox](http://127.0.0.1:4000) and run the [frame list query](./src/bff/README.md).

### Backend metrics

- Open [Prometheus Targets](http://127.0.0.1:9091/targets) and wait for the
  `frame-inventory-backend` target to show **UP**. It scrapes
  `http://backend:8080/actuator/prometheus` on the Compose network.
- Open [Grafana](http://127.0.0.1:3001), sign in with the initial credentials
  above, and run `up{job="frame-inventory-backend"}` in **Explore** using the
  default Prometheus data source. A value of `1` confirms the backend is being scraped.
- Open [Frame Inventory Backend](http://127.0.0.1:3001/d/frame-inventory-backend/frame-inventory-backend)
  for HTTP and gRPC request rate, errors, p50, p95, and p99 latency, and resource saturation.
  Generate API traffic and allow at least two Prometheus scrapes for request graphs
  to populate.
- The **Frame inventory activity** section shows committed creates, updates, and
  soft deletes, plus successful gRPC reads and version conflicts. The totals cover
  the dashboard time range. Rejected or rolled-back writes and repeated deletes
  that change no data are excluded from the totals.

Prometheus and Grafana listen on localhost. Their named volumes keep metrics
and Grafana settings across restarts.

### BFF metrics

Run `docker compose up -d --build bff prometheus grafana`. If Prometheus was
already running, reload its scrape configuration with
`docker compose restart prometheus`. Confirm that `frame-inventory-bff` is
**UP** in [Prometheus Targets](http://127.0.0.1:9091/targets). Prometheus scrapes
`http://bff:9465/metrics` on the Compose network.

Open [Frame Inventory BFF](http://127.0.0.1:3001/d/frame-inventory-bff/frame-inventory-bff)
for GraphQL request rate, error percentage, p50/p95/p99 latency, in-flight
requests, and event loop utilization. The **Slowest queries and mutations (p95)**
panel ranks top-level fields such as `frames` and `updateFrame` by resolver
latency over the selected time range. Run the [frame list query](./src/bff/README.md)
several times across at least two scrapes. Run `{ frames(page: -1) { page } }`
to generate a GraphQL error. The dashboard counts GraphQL errors even when
Apollo responds with HTTP 200.

### Backend and BFF logs

Run `docker compose up -d --build bff grafana`. Alloy reads the backend and
BFF containers’ stdout and stderr through the Docker socket and sends them
to Loki. Loki stores logs in the `loki-data` volume with seven-day retention.
For a failed GraphQL request, take the `X-Correlation-Id` response header
and search both services with
`{service_name=~"backend|bff"} | json | correlationId="your-id"`.
For a production deployment, configure log storage, retention, and access
controls for that environment.

Open [Grafana Explore](http://127.0.0.1:3001/explore), select **Loki**,
and switch to **Code** mode to run either LogQL query.

- Backend — `{service_name="backend"}`
- BFF — `{service_name="bff"}`

### OpenTelemetry Collector

Run `docker compose up -d --build otel-collector` to start the Collector and its
dependencies. The Collector scrapes `http://backend:8080/actuator/prometheus`
every 15 seconds and exposes the latest samples on localhost. Once the backend
is ready and the first scrape completes, check for a JVM metric from Spring Boot.

```bash
curl --fail --silent --show-error http://127.0.0.1:9464/metrics | rg '^jvm_memory_used_bytes\{'
```

# Frame Inventory

Monorepo scaffold for the frame-inventory take-home exercise.

## System Overview

The Next.js page calls the Spring Boot health endpoint through a same-origin rewrite. Docker Compose runs both modules alongside PostgreSQL, OpenSearch, OpenSearch Dashboards, Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, Alloy, and the OpenTelemetry Collector. The exercise provides a legacy export in `data/inventory_frame.csv` and describes the inventory features in `INSTRUCTIONS.md`.

Bring the whole stack up with one command.

```bash
docker compose up --build
```

Once PostgreSQL is healthy, the backend applies pending Flyway migrations during startup.

If you have `just` installed, run `just` to list the available recipes.

    14	- A newer source timestamp creates a version. An equal timestamp and matching content hash is a no-op. An older timestamp produces STALE_RECORD. ## Service boundaries

- This package is a standalone Apollo Server 5 service written in strict
  TypeScript. Use Node.js 22 and npm to match Docker and GitHub Actions.
- Apollo owns the GraphQL contract, pagination input validation, and translation
  of gRPC responses and errors. Keep inventory rules and persistence in Spring Boot.
- Use Apollo Sandbox directly at `http://127.0.0.1:4000/`. The Next.js application
  has its own entry point. See [README.md](./README.md) for a sample query.

## Schema and generated types

- Put GraphQL SDL in `schema/*.gql` and resolver implementations in
  `src/resolvers/`. `src/server.ts` loads the SDL with
  `@graphql-tools/load-files` and wires the resolvers into Apollo.
- Use the generated `Resolvers` type for resolver maps. GraphQL Codegen reads the
  same SDL as Apollo. `codegen.yml` maps GraphQL `Frame` to the generated gRPC
  output type.
- Use the [backend's frames.proto](../backend/src/main/proto/frameinventory/v1/frames.proto)
  as the Protobuf source of truth. Keep 64-bit version IDs as strings across
  the gRPC and GraphQL boundary.
- Regenerate files in `src/generated/` with `npm run generate`. The build also
  copies the canonical `frames.proto` to `dist/proto/frames.proto` for the
  runtime gRPC client.

## Validate resolver inputs

- Validate the allowed ranges and combinations of GraphQL arguments at the
  resolver boundary before making an upstream call. Keep these checks aligned
  with Spring's contract and preserve omission where Spring supplies a default.
- For each validation rule, test a valid boundary and a rejected value. Check
  that invalid input returns `BAD_USER_INPUT` and leaves the gRPC stub uncalled.
- `frames(page: Int, size: Int)` calls Spring's `ListFrames` RPC and returns
  `items`, `page`, `size`, and `hasNext`. Reject negative pages and sizes
  outside `1–50` before calling gRPC. Treat omitted or null arguments as unset
  so Spring applies page `0` and size `25`.
- The remaining operations are `frame`, `frameHistory`, `createFrame`,
  `updateFrame`, and `deleteFrame`. Pass expected version IDs to gRPC as
  positive 64-bit integer strings. An update replaces writable attributes.
- Throw `GraphQLError` with an `extensions.code` from `src/consts.ts`.
  The shared mapping in `src/frame-client.ts` uses `BAD_USER_INPUT` for
  `INVALID_ARGUMENT`, `NOT_FOUND` for missing frames, `ALREADY_EXISTS` for
  reserved IDs, `CONFLICT` for gRPC `ABORTED`, `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` for
  `UNAVAILABLE` or `DEADLINE_EXCEEDED`, and `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR` for
  unexpected failures.

## Logging and retries

- Cockatiel 3 supports the BFF's CommonJS build and Jest setup. Read-only RPCs
  retry only `UNAVAILABLE`, at most twice with 100 ms backoff. Every attempt
  shares the same five-second gRPC deadline. Send each mutation once.
- Use the shared Pino logger in `src/logger.ts` for structured service logs.
  Use `logger.info` for service lifecycle events such as startup. Use
  `logger.debug` for request-level diagnostics such as RPC duration or retry
  attempt number. Pino defaults to `info`. Set the logger level to `debug`
  when troubleshooting locally.
- Put diagnostic values in structured fields. Keep request payloads,
  credentials, and frame IDs out of logs. Log upstream status codes for service
  failures and keep client error messages generic for unexpected failures.
- Inspect Compose logs with `docker compose logs bff` from the repository root.

## Run and verify

- From the repository root, start the Compose service with
  `docker compose up --build bff`. The multi-stage image builds the code and
  packages its output, SDL, and production dependencies for the runtime stage.
- For a local run, start Spring, then run `npm ci`, `npm run build`, and
  `npm start` from `src/bff`. Set `FRAME_GRPC_ENDPOINT` as `host:port` when
  overriding the default of `localhost:9090` locally or `backend:9090` in

- From `src/bff`, run `npm run format:check`, `npm run lint`, and `npm test`.

  [BFF workflow](../../.github/workflows/bff-checks.yml) runs the checks on pull
  requests and pushes to `main`.

  `executeOperation` with a stub gRPC client to check GraphQL data, error codes,
  and which calls reach Spring. `npm test` generates types, type-checks the
  tests, and runs them through ts-jest.
